children: A trading ban in India on JPMorgan Chase's
Mauritius unit was lifted after the company surrendered 29.6M rupees (or $311,230) tied to an index manipulation charge, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg News.

Copthall Mauritius Investment, along with India-based Mansi Share and Stock Broking, deposited alleged unlawful gains last month after an interim order by the Securities and Exchange Board, the report noted.

The gains were related to trades in the closing auction session on the BSE (Bombay Stock Exchange) on Aug. 13, according to one of the sources, who asked not to be identified, as the information is private.
While the trading ban on both companies have been lifted, SEBI's investigation is expected to continue, Bloomberg reported.
The regulator is planning to give each of the companies an in-person hearing as part of the investigation, the source reportedly said.
